Subject: Prowess offer: conditional buyout vs onboarding credits

Stephanie / Jonas —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. After digging with finance, legal and our deployment team, we can move on a replacement-package that balances your migration risk with our commitment to grow together. High level proposition below: 

- Conditional buyout: $180k one-time credit applied to the customer account. 60% of that ($108k) is available as an upfront account credit on go-live. The remaining 40% ($72k) is held in escrow and becomes non-refundable if usage ramps to >70% of the committed MRR within 6 months. If ramp doesn't hit the threshold, that 40% converts to pro-rated onboarding credits valid for 12 months.
- Implementation credits: additional $25k of technical services credits, valid for 9 months, to cover configs, connectors and runbook creation.
- Dedicated onboarding engineer for up to 8 weeks (4 days/week).

We believe this structure reduces your downside while preserving a durable commercial alignment (we both benefit if usage grows). Attached is a draft sideletter and a quick cost sheet showing how the credit amortization would flow in our billing system.

If that looks directionally right, we can work with legal to get a short sideletter and SLA that limits the refundable portion to the 6-month ramp metric. Happy to adjust the ramp threshold or timing.

Best,
Max Chen
Head of Partnerships, Prowess.ai

Max —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the docs. A few immediate thoughts from our side: 

1) Implementation risk: our main concern is the unexpected integration work (Auth, event pipelines, and a custom embedder). We'd like the onboarding credits to be scoped explicitly to non-recurring implementation work (connectors, runbooks, playbook testing).

2) Ramp metric: 70% of committed MRR in 6 months feels aggressive for a customer of this size if they have non-trivial integration work. Can we consider a 9-month window or a lower threshold (60%)?

3) Refund mechanics: we need a clean accounting path if they don't hit the ramp (how the escrow converts to credits, ledger treatment). Also need to cap any open-ended egress or third-party bills.

4) Sideletter: we appreciate a short sideletter, but legal will want the exact trigger language and an exit clause if either party materially breaches core SLAs.

We'd like to propose an alternate blend: $120k upfront credit + $60k escrowed refundable buyout (subject to 60% ramp in 9 months) + $30k implementation credits (9 months) + a bounded onboarding engineer commitment (6 weeks). This reduces vendor exposure while giving them more runway.

Can you run the numbers on that and share a clean sideletter draft that covers: ramp metric, refund conversion path, credits expiry, and cap on pass-through costs?

If we can close on terms this week we can route for approval.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Max's note and Stephanie's ask. Quick internal take before we go back: 

Summary: Prowess is offering a performance-tied buyout plus implementation credits. Stephanie countered with a shallower upfront + longer ramp.

My recommended approach (to support Stephanie's counter, while protecting our P&L):

- Accept a blended structure but push refundability into a usage-cliff tied to both MRR and a technical readiness checklist (three items: successful SSO test, event sync within 48h lag, basic embedder throughput). This reduces 'fake' ramp claims.
- Move the escrow timeline to 9 months but keep refundable portion to 30-40% (we can authorize up to $72k refundable only if legal signs off).
- Increase onboarding credits to $30k but make them specifically for non-recurring implementation (one-time use). Any additional hours billed at standard TS rates.
- Add an operational egress cap of $5k for third-party pass-through in the first 6 months.

Attachment: implementation-costs.xlsx shows the cost/run-rate impact for these options. If we accept the $120k/$60k structure (Stephanie's suggestion), our expected NRR impact in year one is ~ -$45k after implementation amortization; acceptable from an ACV protection stance.

If everyone agrees I can draft the negotiation bullets for Max and ask legal to pre-draft the sideletter language around the tech-readiness checklist.

—Jonas

Stephanie / Jonas —

Appreciate the thoughtful feedback. We spoke with our finance and legal teams this morning and can accept the blended approach with the following refinements: 

- Commercial: $120k upfront account credit; $60k escrowed refundable portion. Refundability triggers on achieving either (A) 60% of committed MRR within 9 months OR (B) successful completion of the tech-readiness checklist (SSO, event lag, embedder throughput) within 9 months. If neither condition is met, the $60k converts to $60k of implementation credits valid for 12 months.
- Onboarding credits: $30k (9 months) specifically for non-recurring implementation tasks.
- Onboarding engineer: we will provide a dedicated engineer for up to 6 weeks (3 days/week) and escalate a priority channel for the first 90 days.
- Egress/pass-through: capped at $5k for the first 6 months; anything beyond requires pre-approval.

We're attaching an updated draft sideletter reflecting this structure. If that looks good, our legal team can produce a DocuSign package and we can aim to execute before month-end.

Thanks —
Max Chen
Head of Partnerships, Prowess.ai
